doc.subject: Vela Freight books three cargo returns; Korsa Launch slips again
doc.verdict: Return cargo is becoming a product line. Korsa Launch lost another month. Buyers are pricing reliability above cost.

items.headline: Vela Freight booked three cargo returns worth $48 million.
paragraphs: Vela Freight signed three return missions with Mirelle Orbital, its first paid bookings for capsules that come back to Earth.
The contracts start in 2031 and include an option for two more flights if the first return lands on schedule.
items.means: Return cargo now has paying customers, so capacity that can fly and land on time is worth more in negotiations.

block.head: How Vela Freight went from test capsule to paid returns
block.lead: Four public steps in six weeks.

points.text: Vela Freight flew its first test capsule.
The capsule landed within the target zone.
Mirelle Orbital said it was in talks for return flights.
Vela Freight announced three paid returns.

items.headline: Korsa Launch moved its first flight to June.
paragraphs: Korsa Launch said engine tests need another month, the third delay this year, and kept its customer list unchanged.

block.head: Korsa Launch's first flight keeps moving right
block.title: Months of delay per announcement (as stated)

items.headline: Two underwriters added reliability clauses to launch cover.
paragraphs: Quorn Mutual and Tessaly Re now price launch cover by the provider's last ten flights instead of a flat rate.
Providers with fewer than ten flights pay a surcharge until they build a record.
items.means: A short flight record now costs money directly, so new providers should budget for higher cover in their first year.

items.headline: Mirelle Orbital switched its ground network to Sorell Relay.
paragraphs: Mirelle Orbital moved station passes from its own dishes to Sorell Relay and said contact time per orbit doubled.
